basis: Peripheral neuropathy with defining optic atrophy (10/10); muscle wasting and vocal cord paresis are neurogenic. Hearing impairment occurs in 1/10.

decisions.pulmonary: none: vocal cord paresis occurs in 4/10 but reflects neural dysfunction rather than direct airway disease.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: muscle wasting and weakness reflect denervation; intrinsic muscle disease or common structural skeletal damage is not established.

basis: Infectious or immune-mediated DIC with defining necrotic purpura; vascular thrombosis occurs in 30-79%. Primary cap prioritizes coagulation, skin and immune mechanism.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: occlusive vascular thrombosis is defining and occurs in 30-79%; the three primary slots prioritize coagulation, skin and immune mechanism.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: necrotic purpuric skin lesions define purpura fulminans; blistering and gangrene occur in 30-79%.

basis: Demyelinating peripheral neuropathy; weakness and wasting are neurogenic. Supplied evidence does not establish fixed skeletal damage in at least 30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: neurogenic weakness and wasting do not establish direct muscle disease; fixed structural foot deformity meeting the 30% threshold is not established.

basis: Defining skeletal abnormalities and developmental disability; laryngomalacia occurs in 30-79%. Omphalocele affects the abdominal wall; feeding symptoms do not establish bowel damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: omphalocele is an abdominal-wall defect without established bowel injury; dysphagia and poor suck do not establish direct gastrointestinal disease.

basis: FGF23 excess causes defining hypophosphatemic osteomalacia and renal phosphate-reabsorption dysfunction (80-99%); nephrocalcinosis may be treatment-related.

decisions.renal: primary: renal phosphate-reabsorption dysfunction is a defining diagnostic component, present in 80-99%; structural renal injury is not required for this primary label.

basis: Primary immunodeficiency; bronchiectasis (30-79%) is a separately diagnosed consequence of recurrent infections. Intestinal lymphoid hyperplasia (30-79%) lacks demonstrated functional damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: bronchiectasis occurs in 30-79% but is a separate disease arising from recurrent infections; direct pulmonary lymphoproliferative injury is not established.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: intestinal lymphoid nodular hyperplasia occurs in 30-79%, but functional impairment or destructive enteropathy at that frequency is not established.

basis: Inclusion-body myopathy and Paget bone disease characterize this subtype; dementia is optional and not established in the supplied HNRNPA1 cohort.

decisions.neurologic: none: despite the generic parent-derived definition, dementia is optional and unreported in the supplied subtype cohort; a characteristic neurologic phenotype is not established.

basis: FG neurodevelopmental syndrome; metopic synostosis and strabismus each occur in the single reported patient (1/1). Chronic constipation alone does not establish bowel damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: chronic constipation is reported in 1/1 patient, but no structural bowel disease or established intrinsic intestinal dysfunction is supplied.

basis: Neurodegeneration with characteristic erythrocyte acanthocytosis; myopathy and muscle-fiber atrophy occur in 30-79%. Oral injury is secondary mechanical trauma from dyskinesia.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: tongue/lip injury is reported in 2/2 but results from mechanical self-trauma due to dyskinesia, rather than direct gastrointestinal disease.

basis: Autoimmune cytopenias, monocytosis and lymphoproliferation define RALD; hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic damage or functional impairment.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatomegaly is characteristic, but enlargement alone does not establish function-impairing infiltration or hepatic injury in at least 30%.
